prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "poetry", with the standing line "A desktop reference notebook where tagged definitions become a searchable, graphable web of writers, titles and terms." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A handwritten definition card at upper left, its prose interrupted by three small bracket tags. A line carries the card into a parser drawn as a narrow comb that lifts the three tags clear of the sentence. From the comb, two arrows descend: one to a stack of record cards holding one entity each, one to a ledger of paired rows joining a source card to a target card. From the ledger, lines fan rightward and downward into a loose web of dots and threads — the same records, now seen as a network with a few heavily connected nodes.

Magnified circles set beside it show circle one, a tag lifted from a sentence and resolving into a named card. circle two, one ledger row showing an arrow from source card to target card. circle three, a typed query filtering a column of records down to a few matches. circle four, a tag whose target does not exist, with an empty card being started beside it.

Colour is used so that One accent marks tags and the links they become. A second accent marks disagreements between text and links. A third accent marks what leaves the database.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 4,980 entities migrated into one table; 3 kinds of reference tag; 7 data-quality reports; 2 export formats; graph draws at most 500 nodes; backups kept 7 days.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: entities, relationships, {w:}, {p:}, {t:}, references, writers, titles, clichés, literary terms, orphans, duplicates, unlinked references, saved searches, command palette, poetry.db.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: definition text, {w:}, {p:}, {t:}, reference parser, entities, relationships, link web, quick create. tag to link, source and target, full-text search, missing referent. unlinked references, duplicates, orphans, missing definitions, unknown tags, unknown types, linked not mentioned. JSON export, Markdown export, graph view, spoken word, daily backup. poetry.db, desktop window, saved searches, command palette.

Set these short notes beside what they explain: One card shape holds writers, titles, terms; Tags in prose become rows of links. Deleting a card deletes its links too; Search accepts and, or, not. Reports find text and links disagreeing; Orphans have no link either way. Exports resolve tags into readable names; Speech needs a key to work. Interface calls the database without a server.
